channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Machado Returns to Venezuela to Urge On Democratic Transition
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Caracas in a surprise move that could pose the biggest test yet to acting President Delcy Rodríguez’s political opening and the Trump administration’s strategy for post-Maduro Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago

item.title: Hassett Says US Close to Deal With Canada as Talks Pick Up
item.description: US trade negotiations with Canada have picked up and are “gathering steam,” White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett says in an interview with Fox News.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: Trump Says Decision Time Nears on Iran: Deal or ‘Finish It Off’
item.description: President Donald Trump said it’s “getting to be decision time” on whether he will make a deal with Tehran or resume attacks as Iranian and Houthi threats against Americans in the Middle East continue to grow.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Iran War Risks Escalation After Elections
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, former US Ambassador to Israel Daniel Shapiro assesses the risk of renewed fighting with Iran after elections in Israel and the US and warns that another round of military operations could deepen regional and global economic strains. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Shapiro examines Israel’s election and argues that a change in Israeli leadership could provide an opportunity to reset a US-Israel relationship that has become increasingly strained. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Italy’s Salvini Wins New League Mandate With Anti-Ukraine Pledge
item.description: Giorgia Meloni ally Matteo Salvini was reelected leader of his far-right party League, part of Italy’s ruling coalition, after he promised to push the government to stop supporting Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Albanese

item.title: Trump Says He Plans More Announcements on Economy
item.description: President Donald Trump says his administration has “many other announcements” to make following his announcement of Volkswagen AG’s plan to build an Audi factory in Georgia.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: Midterm Fight Intensifies in Final Campaign Stretch
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, CBS News White House and political correspondent Ed O’Keefe and Puck Washington writer Abby Livingston examine the final days of the US midterm campaign as candidates, former presidents and outside groups pour resources into key battlegrounds. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, O’Keefe and Livingston discuss tightening races, the impact of massive political spending and whether increasingly provocative campaign tactics will motivate or alienate voters. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Crenshaw Presses Musk on Starlink for Ukraine
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Republican Rep. Dan Crenshaw of Texas calls for expanding Ukraine’s access to Starlink over Russia and increasing pressure on Vladimir Putin to create leverage for peace negotiations. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Crenshaw also discusses President Donald Trump’s Russia policy, the US midterms and his concerns about social media’s influence on American politics as he prepares to leave Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israel Election Tests Netanyahu’s Hold on Power
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert discusses how security, democracy and the war in Iran are shaping Israel’s election and argues that the country needs a change in its approach to settler violence in the West Bank. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Olmert also examines how the US midterms could affect the US-Israel relationship and says decisions about further military action against Iran should be based on intelligence rather than electoral politics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Epstein Haunts GOP in Midterms as Democrats Vow Fresh Probes
item.description: President Donald Trump can’t shake the furor over Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Musk’s Money Reshapes the Midterm Spending Race
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Corporate Lobbying and Influence Reporter Emily Birnbaum explains how Elon Musk’s record political giving is boosting Republican groups in the final days before the US midterms. Bloomberg News reports Musk has now contributed more than $445 million to political groups this election cycle, putting him among the biggest political contributors ever. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Birnbaum examines Republicans’ advantage in outside spending and Democrats’ strength in direct candidate fundraising, which can make their advertising dollars go further. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Higher Energy Costs Weigh on Trump’s Midterm Pitch
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Financial Times Associate Editor and Sea Change author Rana Foroohar explains how the Iran war and higher energy costs are shaping voters’ economic concerns ahead of the US midterms. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Foroohar also examines America’s competition with China and Russia over shipping, infrastructure and influence in a rapidly changing Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brian Fitzpatrick Faces Tough Pennsylvania House Race Despite Trump Distance
item.description: For one Pennsylvania Republican, winning reelection to the US House in a suburban Philadelphia seat likely hinges on his long-standing effort to keep President Donald Trump at arm’s length.
item.dc:creator: Liz Skalka

item.title: Brazil’s Presidential Race Comes Down to the Wire
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Brazil Country Chief Filipe Pacheco explains how turnout, public security and the economy are shaping the razor-thin presidential runoff between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Pacheco examines Lula’s last-minute push to mobilize voters through social media and what the election could mean for the future of Latin America’s largest economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Presidential Election 2026 Live Updates: Lula, Bolsonaro Vie for Voters
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: US and Israel Elections Loom Over Iran War
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Defense Lead Becca Wasser and Bloomberg News Middle East correspondent Dan Williams examine how elections in the US and Israel could shape the next phase of the Iran war, including the possibility of renewed US strikes after the midterms. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Wasser and Williams assess potential US military options, Iran’s capacity to retaliate and the political calculations facing President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK’s Rayner Defends Burnham Move to Revisit EU Free Movement
item.description: Housing Secretary Angela Rayner denied that Andy Burnham is reopening the Brexit debate by reconsidering a key manifesto pledge to rule out freedom of movement with the European Union, saying the prime minister is simply seeking an “honest conversation” about Britain’s future relationship with the bloc.
item.dc:creator: Eamon Akil Farhat

item.title: France Protests: Tough Security Measures Help Avoid Violence at Demonstrations
item.description: France avoided a repeat of large-scale violence and looting that marred nationwide protests a week ago, suggesting the government’s decision to boost police numbers and contain marches paid off.
item.dc:creator: James Regan

item.title: Serb Strongman Faces New Rival in Watershed Vote: What to Watch
item.description: Serbians go to polls to decide whether longtime strongman Aleksandar Vucic will return as prime minister or be ousted by unprecedented student-led opposition that wants to crack down on graft and boost democracy.
item.dc:creator: Misha Savic

item.title: VW Plans New Audi Plant in Georgia, Handing Trump a Win
item.description: Volkswagen AG plans to build a new $4 billion factory for its premium Audi brand in the southern US state of Georgia, expecting the move will yield potential relief from tariffs that have severely eroded profits.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Coppola, Josh Wingrove and William Wilkes
